messages:
noah: quick update 1: we just pushed Ripple Packer to a small canary (5 instances, ~8% traffic). this is the micropacking change that opportunistically merges short concurrent requests into rolling micro-batches.
noah: config highlights: consolidation_window_ms=12, max_micropack=32, short-bypass-threshold=16
deploy-bot: canary deploy 1722223333 -> healthy on 5 hosts :white_check_mark:
lin: any bench numbers yet? curious about p50 vs p99 tradeoffs.
noah: ran a 15min sweep across three seq profiles. quick paste of the trimmed summary:
noah: ```
noah: ./bench.sh --model=redwood-medium --seq=64 --qps=800 --warmup=60
noah: baseline: p50=210ms, p95=540ms, p99=900ms, cost/unit=1.00
noah: ripple-canary: p50=148ms, p95=520ms, p99=905ms, cost/unit=0.82
noah: delta: p50 -29.5%, cost -18%, p99 ~flat
noah: 
noah: ./bench.sh --model=redwood-medium --seq=16 --qps=2000
noah: baseline: p50=95ms, p95=320ms, p99=580ms, cost/unit=1.00
noah: ripple-canary: p50=78ms, p95=315ms, p99=590ms, cost/unit=0.90
noah: delta: p50 -17.9%, cost -10%, slight p99 up on very bursty micro workloads
noah: ```
emma: solid p50 wins. any regressions on extremely latency-sensitive tiny requests?
noah: saw a ~5-8% p50 regression for seq<=8 in one micro-burst test; added a short-bypass for requests < short-bypass-threshold to skip micropack. patch queued.
tariq: did packing affect KV cache eviction patterns or GPU memory spikes?
noah: we observed slightly higher short-lived GPU memory allocations during pack assembly but peak memory stayed under limits. KV hitrate was stable once we capped consolidation_window_ms.
lin: what's the rollout plan? ops constraints?
noah: ramp plan: 8% -> 25% after 45m if error and retry metrics stable, then -> 60% next 3h, final -> 100% over 12h. emergency rollback in 3 clicks via the traffic router.
emma: please add an alert for queue_depth > 2x baseline and retry_rate > 1.5x.
noah: added both alerts and a minimal runbook. doc: https://go/redwood/ripple-packer-rollout
deploy-bot: ramp: 8% -> 25% at 1722223433 :rocket:
lin: infra note: GPU utilization smoother, fewer tiny kernels firing; looks good from node perspective.
noah: also landed a small kernel selection tweak that prefers the fused_attention for micropacked groups; gives another ~5% cost on micro-heavy slices.
emma: can we get a 1-slide blurb for the weekly all-hands? ops win + econ bullets.
noah: will DM a draft in #all-hands-slides. thanks to lin and tariq for the infra testing and to emma for the alerting help.
tariq: nice work team :tada:
deploy-bot: final ramp to 100% scheduled at 1722223477 1: monitoring window open :eyes:
